The document concerns archival materials from the Swiss representation in Los Angeles, which are part of the Swiss Federal Archives holdings managed by the national archives of Switzerland based in Bern.

These records document the activities and correspondence of the Swiss diplomatic mission in Los Angeles over several decades, reflecting Switzerland's international relations and administrative practices.

The Swiss Federal Archives, under the direction of Philippe Künzler since 2018, is responsible for preserving, cataloging, and providing access to such archival materials for historical research and transparency.

Related finding aids include E2200.222 for the Swiss representation in Galatz (1947/1970) and E2200.302A for the Swiss representation in Vesoul (2009), both serving as administrative indexes for archival deposits.

The Los Angeles records are part of a broader network of Swiss diplomatic archives in the United States, alongside the Washington mission records documented in Aktenverzeichnisse (1909/1910), illustrating Switzerland's diplomatic presence and administrative continuity across different locations and time periods.
